decisions.reason: As part of a visibly launched organic cold-cuts push, this product benefits from sunk certification and distribution investments and management can still blame any weak sales on temporary post-launch and pandemic-related effects.
This organic line extension fits the same publicly signaled bio strategy, so a large incumbent manufacturer would be inclined to continue rather than admit the launch underperformed.
The firm has already committed to the organic sliced-meat range and is likely to persist with this variant unless results are clearly poor, which can still be framed as temporary market noise.
This exotic deli-counter aspic specialty looks more like a peripheral experiment than a core strategic product, so despite some escalation pressures it is the easiest item to discontinue.
Its own product page suggests a relatively visible commitment, and management is therefore somewhat more likely to continue supporting it rather than reverse course quickly.
This pâté variant appears less central to the firm's broader strategic direction than the organic launches, so the commitment effect is weaker and discontinuation becomes slightly more likely.
